to_canonical()¶

converts the rule to a standardized “canonoical” form by rotating cube types, changing cube type order, and color ordering This is useful for comparing rules that have the same pattern of interactions expressed in different color enumerations and cube type rotations function written in part by catGPT but I had to refise heavily

Return type:

PolycubesRule

polycube_util.py¶

This module contains high-level utility functions for polyccubes that don’t require a polycubes binary but do require other polycubeutil modules. Specifically, it requires the classes PolycubesStructure, PolycubeStructureCube, and PolycubesRule from polycube_structure.py, polycubesRule.py, and cube.py respectively.

pypatchy.polycubeutil.polycube_util.make_colors_consecutive(rule)¶

translation of Joakim Bohlin’s simplify method from utils.js Simplifies a rule by making colors consecutive (so colors used in rule will be 1, 2, 3, etc.)

Parameters:

rule (PolycubesRule) – a polycubes rule

Raises:

AssertionError – if the rule has patches with color value of zero

Returns:

the rule, simplified

Return type:

PolycubesRule

pypatchy.polycubeutil.polycube_util.get_fully_addressable_rule(structure)¶

Given a topology (as a FiniteLatticeStructure object), construct a polycubes structure where each location in the topology is a unique cube type, and each connection between two locations is mediated by a unique color. :param structure: the topology (as a FiniteLatticeStructure object) :return: A polycube of the topology with non-repeating cube types and colors :rtype: PolycubesStructure

Parameters:

structure (FiniteLatticeStructure)

Return type:

PolycubeStructure
